headline: 29 trades, net -1.5 bps/bet (gross ~+1.4 vs ~+4 hoped); last-10 window gross now -2.1. Thin. Flat now.
alert_message: Recent 10-bet window turned gross-negative (-2.1 bps); overall gross edge (~+1.4) still well below the ~4 bps hoped. Small sample, keep watching.
regime_note: BTC ~$86k, still well above the old $76–82k range — a trending/breakout backdrop that is generally unfavorable for a mean-reversion fade. Signal is flat (0), nothing live right now.
assessment_md:
**How it's doing.** Over 29 resolved trades the strategy is averaging **-1.5 bps per bet** (total -44.9 bps). Stripping out the assumed 3 bps cost, the *gross* edge is only about **+1.4 bps/bet** — positive, but far short of the ~4 bps we hoped for and below the ~3.9 bps needed just to break even. Win rate is 37.9%; that's fine for a fade strategy if the wins are bigger than the losses, but here they aren't paying enough.

**What changed vs last time.** The rolling window shifted from 13 bets (gross ~+0.6) to the latest 10 bets, where gross has slipped to **-2.1 bps** (net -5.1). So the most recent stretch is not just cost-eaten — it's gross-negative, an early yellow flag.

**What the numbers do and don't tell us.** With only 29 trades, and a signal that trades ~1-2% of candles, this is still a **small sample**. Individual outcomes swing wildly (from -28 to +49 bps), so both the good and bad windows are noisy. We cannot yet say the edge is broken — but we also have zero evidence it's net-profitable. Separately, the edge search found **0 survivors** meeting the profitability bar on both venues.

**Bottom line.** Marginal-at-best, currently underwater, in a regime (trending, above old range) that works against mean reversion. No profit is implied or guaranteed. Keep it running in monitor-only mode; don't add size.
